title: `COMMENT ON EXTENSION xxx` in Structure.sql causing problems when loading db on Heroku and other services
body:
### Steps to reproduce
<!-- (Guidelines for creating a bug report are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#creating-a-bug-report)) -->

### Expected behavior
<!-- Tell us what should happen -->
We should be able to run `rake db:structure:load` without any trouble on any server where you can run `rake db:schema:load` without issues. 

### Actual behavior
<!-- Tell us what happens instead -->
the rake `db:structure:load` fails on the line `COMMENT ON EXTENSION plpgsql IS 'PL/pgSQL procedural language';`

[More of an explanation here (essentially super user access is not available)](https://help.heroku.com/AHH2KNSR/why-do-i-get-postgres-extension-errors-when-i-run-rake-db-structure-load-or-rake-db-setup) this also tends to happen on amazon RDS where super user access is similarly not available. However running `rake db:schema:load` on the same system would seem to work just fine. 

### Other Notes
The only reason I decided to file this is that I just noticed [a precedent for it in this Pull request](https://github.com/aripollak/rails/commit/df050484cd3b5e888b50d2e0554a4077407459a8)

I think it would be a good fix to strip out those comments from structure.sql because ... 

- they don't seem to add anything to the db:structure:load process, but are added since [Rails seems to shell out to pg:dump to create them](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/master/activerecord/lib/active_record/tasks/postgresql_database_tasks.rb#L78) and the rest of structure.sql
- generated schema.rb seems to do just fine without them

### System configuration
**Rails version**:
6.0 RC1

**Ruby version**:
2.6.3
